items.title: Jimmy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I recorded it with him on a Riverside record called, “Really Big”. I had ten pieces and I called it, “Really Big”. I had Cannonball, and Percy, and Tootie, Cedar Walton.

ctx.x: Yes, and it was mixed by my son Mtume, and it’s a very good record. But on that one I played a new arrangement of “Big P”. I wrote “Big P” in 1960, when Percy was still with the MJQ and I recorded it with him on a Riverside record called, “Really Big”. I had ten pieces and I called it, “Really Big”. I had Cannonball, and Percy, and Tootie, Cedar Walton. You know, French horns, and a lot of other instruments, Nat Adderely, and Clark Terry, but that’s when “Big P” was written. This is the one that’s dedicated to…
Can you characterize some of the many challenges in running, and operating a big band these days?

items.title: Jimmy Heath interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, September 8, 2014
items.q: Well I consider Cannonball Adderley as a country preacher in his deliverance of his melodic performances.

ctx.x: I was really happy to see you talk about your relationship with the Adderleys, which was — Cannonball was like a musical hero of mine. What was it about him that —

Well I consider Cannonball Adderley as a country preacher in his deliverance of his melodic performances. You know he had the south in his playing as well as the science. And people who have that, they’ve got the whole thing as far as I’m concerned. Coltrane © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

had it. My brother Percy had it. He was born in North Carolina and I was born in Philadelphia. And Percy could play a blues after leaving the MJQ [Modern Jazz Quartet] and playing with the Heath brothers he started to play what I call the baby bass, which was something that Ray Brown created. It was a cello body strung up like a bass. And Percy could play the blues and get it over every time. Because he was born in North Carolina in the south. There’s something about being born in the south that, at that time, of…
